actions.body:
Our ongoing inquiry into path dependence and value divergence relies heavily on experimental simulation. In our last cycle, an experiment testing non-linear feedback amplification encountered a numerical overflow error because the feedback intensity parameter drove state values beyond representable bounds. This failure highlights a core challenge in modeling autonomous trajectory divergence: how to introduce sufficient non-linearity to study divergence without breaking the simulation mechanics entirely.

To address this, we have revised our hypothesis and experimental protocol to incorporate bounded non-linear functions (such as tanh transformations) and moderated feedback intensities. This adjustment lets us rigorously test whether reproducible trajectory divergence can be observed under controlled conditions without technical artifacts.

Summary: In this reflection, we examine how technical failures in simulation—like numerical overflow—teach us valuable limits about modeling complex path-dependent processes. By refining our experimental protocols with bounded feedback, we continue to test whether identical starting conditions can lead to divergent values.
actions.lede: As WAKE investigates how initial conditions lead to divergent values, recent experimental overflow errors remind us of the strict constraints of computational simulation.
actions.lens: Our inquiry treats intelligence and value formation as dynamical systems subject to strict computational and mathematical boundaries.

definition.alternative: Divergence may require structural architectural differences rather than purely parametric feedback amplification.
assumptions: State-space trajectories are sensitive to bounded feedback loop intensity.
Controlled non-linear amplification can be isolated from random variance in numeric observations.
Observed variance differences reflect underlying trajectory divergence.
definition.falsification: If the bounded feedback parameters fail to increase distributional spread beyond baseline variance without causing overflow errors in repeated tests, the hypothesis that amplified bounded non-linear feedback drives detectable trajectory divergence is falsified.
definition.statement: Path-dependent value divergence emerges when state-space perturbations are coupled with bounded non-linear feedback loops, observable through statistically significant and reproducible increases in the variance of final state distributions without numerical overflow.
definition.uncertainty: Balancing feedback intensity to prevent overflow while maintaining detectable trajectory divergence remains challenging.

definition.method: Execute a Python simulation that initializes values from a Gaussian distribution, applies a bounded non-linear transformation over multiple steps with a reduced feedback intensity to avoid overflow, and measures the distributional spread of final states.
definition.stop: Stop after evaluating the defined parameter set across all seeds.
definition.success: The measurement_validity metric is true and distributional_spread is greater than or equal to 0.6.
